# Test 'commit split' for a non-HEAD commit using rebase.

[!unix] skip # pending github.com/creack/pty/pull/155
[!git:2.45] skip # git add -p output is fixed to Git version

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2024-07-08T05:04:32Z'

# setup
cd repo
git init
git commit --allow-empty -m 'Initial commit'
gs repo init
# This fork uses merge-based restacking by default;
# pin the rebase method to preserve this script's original behavior.
git config spice.restack.method rebase


# Create a branch with 3 commits
git add file1.txt
gs bc -m 'Commit 1' feature

git add file2a.txt file2b.txt
gs cc -m 'Commit 2 (to be split)'

git add file3.txt
gs cc -m 'Commit 3'

# Show log before split
git log --oneline -3

# Split commit 2 (not HEAD) - using HEAD~1 to reference it.
# The terminal dump is not compared in full:
# input echo position in the pty is timing-dependent.
# The resulting git state is verified below instead.
with-term -final exit $WORK/input.txt -- gs commit split -m 'Commit 2a' HEAD~1
stdout 'Select hunks for commit 1'
stdout 'Select hunks for commit 2'
stdout 'No hunks selected, stopping split'

# Verify log shows 4 commits total
git log --oneline feature
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/log.txt

-- repo/file1.txt --
file 1 content

-- repo/file2a.txt --
file 2a content

-- repo/file2b.txt --
file 2b content

-- repo/file3.txt --
file 3 content

-- input.txt --
# First iteration: select file2a, quit at file2b
await file2a
snapshot first
feed y\r
clear
await file2b
snapshot second
feed q\r
clear
# Second iteration: quit immediately to commit remainder
await file2b
snapshot third
feed q\r
await
-- golden/log.txt --
1a9b02c Commit 3
d9ce374 Commit 2 (to be split)
551fb3b Commit 2a
312f3f3 Commit 1
2123b73 Initial commit
